key_insight: A cognitively grounded small-language-model framework can generate more realistic SUD patient dialogue by aligning responses with latent patient states like beliefs, coping strategies, and readiness for change.
clinical_relevance: This approach could support more clinically coherent, privacy-conscious, and deployable dialogue systems for counseling workflows in resource-constrained healthcare settings.
method: Detects cognitive components from patient history and counselor questions
Uses knowledge distillation, preference optimization, and attention-guided reward shaping
Generates dialogue aligned to the detected cognitive state rather than generic responses
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improvements across BERTScore, ROUGE, METEOR, BLEU, and LLM-as-judge hit metrics versus generic instruction-tuned baselines and mental-health SLMs, with especially strong gains for open-ended cognitive components.
watch_item: Performance is reported from automatic and LLM-based metrics in an abstract; real-world clinical safety, robustness, and patient impact still need prospective validation.
paper_title: Multi-Objective Aligned Small Language Model Framework for SUD Patient Dialogue Generation
